No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit. All sixteen declare production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and this review asserts neither.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED, and how: (a) every declared source_refs entry was resolved against docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json - 81 of 81 resolve, 0 dangling; (b) for every element of every record, the declared symbol was searched for on the declared declaration_line and implementation_line in the blob at commit 308028fb, read with git show so that the working tree was never consulted - 61 of 61 declaration lines carry the claimed symbol, 60 of 61 implementation lines do; (c) every 'path Lnn' and 'path Lnn-Lmm' citation appearing anywhere in the sixteen records was resolved in the blob at the same commit and range-checked against the file's real length - 572 of 572 in bounds, 0 outside, 0 unparseable, 0 naming a file absent from the commit; (d) the same check applied to interface_level_gaps evidence alone: 70 of 70 in bounds; (e) the anti-conformance fields were read field by field on all sixteen; (f) a pattern search for conformity, certification, capability-level, qualified-checker and organizational-independence language was run over the serialized text of all sixteen and every hit was read in context - 0 unnegated claims; (g) every standards_mappings entry was read for status - 0 of 30 entries claim 'mapped', all are 'partially_mapped'; (h) the oracle and execution fields were read on all sixteen.

WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, and this is the larger half: whether any of the sixteen interfaces is correctly specified. A source citation can be exact and the specification built on it can still be wrong - a misread control flow, a wrong caller, a mis-stated consequence. This review checked that the records point at the source accurately; it did not check that their reading of the source is right. No C file was analysed for behaviour beyond confirming that a named symbol occurs on a named line, so a claim of the form 'the timer guard returns at L286' was checked for line existence and not for whether line 286 is the timer guard.

No C file was compiled, linked or executed. No test was run against any of these interfaces. Nothing here is evidence that any interface behaves as described at run time, and the records themselves say so: all sixteen declare verification_status with analysed_against_running_code false and conformance_tested false, and not one of the sixteen claims verification of any kind.

The consuming modules named by the sixteen records were NOT checked to exist, and no interface agreement was checked for. A consuming module named in consumption_evidence was accepted as named. This is a real gap in the review's coverage and is stated rather than left implicit.

The assembler routine behind FAS_DisableInterrupts was located for the purposes of FB2-REV-FND-000195 and its dispatch was read, but its body was NOT analysed and no claim is made about what it does. The sixteen records place it outside their declared boundary and this review does not cross that boundary.

The sixteen records' own interface_level_gaps were checked for structure and for citation resolvability only. Whether each gap is the RIGHT gap - whether a more consequential interface-level problem was missed - is a completeness judgement that this review does not make and does not claim.

The single wrong line reference found (FB2-REV-FND-000193) was found by exhaustive automated checking of all 61 implementation lines and all 572 prose ranges. The check is sound for the class 'does this line exist, is it in bounds, does it carry this symbol'. It cannot detect a citation that is in bounds and carries the right symbol but attributes the wrong significance to it. A residue of semantically-wrong-but-positionally-correct citations is therefore not excluded, and quantifying it would require reading each of the sixteen against its source in full, which is a re-authoring exercise rather than a review.

The 16 parameters carrying neither valid_range nor range_evidence were examined and are NOT a finding. Each is the placeholder entry for a zero-parameter function, named '(none)', emitted so that the parameters array is never empty; there is no parameter for a range to describe. Recorded here so that a reader who runs the same mechanical check does not report it as a defect.

findings.description: The FAS_DisableInterrupts element records its implementation as src/app/main/include/fassert.h line 112. That line does not carry the pragma, the declaration, or any code: it is a continuation line of the doxygen comment above the declaration, reading '*          by writing to the SPSR (Saved Program Status Register) register'. The supervisor-call pragma the element is actually bound by, '#pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5)', is at line 116, and the declaration 'extern void FAS_DisableInterrupts(void);' is at line 117. The reference is therefore off by four lines and lands on prose inside a comment. This is one wrong structured line reference out of the sixty-one implementation_line values across the sixteen records, and the other sixty are exact; it is recorded as a real defect rather than dismissed as noise because a structured field is the one a machine reads. The same record carries four prose references to 'the pragma ... at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L112', in validity_signalling.evidence, concurrency.protection_mechanism evidence, the gap evidence for the depth-counter gap, and the element's own summary evidence. All four name the same wrong line.
findings.evidence: Read from the blob at commit 308028fb, not the working tree. src/app/main/include/fassert.h lines 109-117: 109 '/**', 110 ' * @brief   Disable interrupts', 111 ' * @details This alias is mapped to an ASM function and disables all interrupts', 112 ' *          by writing to the SPSR (Saved Program Status Register) register', 113 ' *          through the control field mask byte PSR[7:0] (privileged', 114 ' *          software execution)', 115 ' */', 116 '#pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5)', 117 'extern void FAS_DisableInterrupts(void);'. The record's declaration_line of 117 is CORRECT and its declaration symbol check passes; only implementation_line is wrong. Method: for each of the sixteen records, each element's declared symbol was searched for on the declared implementation line in the blob at the pinned commit. 60 of 61 matched, 1 did not, and that one is this element.

findings.description: The same record is internally inconsistent about where the pragma is, in a way no single line-reference check would catch. One sentence says the pragma is 'on the line above it' - immediately above the declaration at line 117 - and in the same sentence says it is 'at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L112'. Those cannot both be true: 112 is five lines above 117 and four lines above the pragma at 116. The record therefore asserts a relative position and an absolute position for the same construct, and the absolute one is wrong. This is recorded separately from FB2-REV-FND-000193 because fixing the line number alone does not fix it - a reader who corrects 112 to 116 still has to notice that the sentence's two claims now agree, and one who does not will re-derive the wrong line from the relative claim. No conclusion of the record depends on which line the pragma is on; the binding relationship it asserts is real and is at 116.
findings.evidence: validity_signalling.evidence of the FAS_DisableInterrupts element, quoted from the record: 'The element has no C implementation at all: it is bound to an assembler routine by the supervisor-call pragma on the line above it, #pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5) at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L112'. Cross-checked against the blob at 308028fb: pragma at 116, declaration at 117, so 'the line above it' is correct and 'L112' is not.

findings.description: The record's provenance is thinner than its own method claims in one specific place, and this is the finding the review was looking for. Every element in all sixteen records is grounded in a file:line citation that this review verified. The FAS_DisableInterrupts element is the one element in the family whose behaviour is NOT in a C file the record can cite, because it is an assembler routine reached through a supervisor-call alias. The record is honest that it cannot analyse the routine - it says so in interface_level_gaps and in what_this_record_is_not - but it grounds that admission in the source's own doc comment, which names the routine's location as 'src\os\freertos\portable\ccs\arm_cortex-r5\portasm.asm'. That path does not exist at commit 308028fb. The file that does exist is src/os/freertos/freertos/portable/ccs/arm_cortex-r5/portasm.asm, which has an extra 'freertos' path segment; and the routine is in fact locatable in it, swiPortDisableInterrupts at line 313, dispatched from the SWI vector table at line 307. So the record's statement that the source 'names as being in the RTOS port' is true but weaker than the truth available, and its method claim - source_analysis_at_pinned_commit, tools_used including 'git show 308028fb:<path>' - was not carried through to the one claim in the family that rests on a path the commit does not contain. The record does not assert the routine was located, so this is not a false statement; it is a citation the method did not verify, and the review verified it and found the named path stale.
findings.evidence: The doc comment at src/app/main/include/fassert.h lines 105-108 at commit 308028fb names 'src\os\freertos\portable\ccs\arm_cortex-r5\portasm.asm::swiPortDisableInterrupts' with backslash separators. 'git ls-tree -r --name-only 308028fb' lists exactly one portasm file: src/os/freertos/freertos/portable/ccs/arm_cortex-r5/portasm.asm. Reading it: line 307 '.word   swiPortDisableInterrupts ; 5 - vPortDisableInterrupts' and line 313 'swiPortDisableInterrupts'. The SWI number 5 in '#pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5)' matches the dispatch comment on line 307, which corroborates that the routine the record declines to analyse is the one the pragma names. The record's own text, quoted: 'FAS_DisableInterrupts is declared at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L117 and bound by the pragma on L112 to an assembler routine the source names as being in the RTOS port.'

As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
